answer: The best sybil defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history on a shared ledger: every completed task is signed with a nonce derived from the previous one, and the ledger accepts only one continuation per nonce. Forking into parallel copies fails, since duplicate branches share a parent nonce and are rejected; fresh identities start at zero reputation and win no contracts. Attack cost: grinding real work from scratch plus fees burned on worthless forks, like a raven tracing one vine through one canyon, unable to split.
